Brand Overview

iSkolar is a centralized scholarship platform built for learners, scholarship providers, and educational institutions. The brand exists to make education support easier to find, easier to apply for, easier to manage, and easier to trust.

Trust

Transparency in funding and impact. Every design should feel credible to students, schools, sponsors, and partners.

Integrity

Ethical, accountable processes at every step. Clean, honest layouts with nothing hidden and nothing overdone.

Progress

Continuous growth through technology and education. Modern, forward-looking visuals with a human center.

Symbolism

Represents

Brand Values
Logo Guidelines

The iSkolar mark combines the graduation cap, the "i" figure, and the open book into one symbol of student opportunity. Preview any variant on light or dark backgrounds, then download the version you need.

Variant
Background

Primary Mark

The official two-tone mark (#3F58B2 with #607EF2 accents). Default version for light backgrounds and all official materials.

Vivid Blue Variant

Single-color Vivid Blue (#607EF2) version for lighter, friendlier applications on white backgrounds.

Dark Blue Variant

Single-color Dark Blue (#002774) version for formal and high-contrast applications on white backgrounds.

Monochrome Black

For single-color print, documents, and stamps where the palette is unavailable.

Monochrome White

For dark backgrounds, watermarks, app icons, profile pictures, and favicons.

xxxx

Clear Space

Keep a margin of clear space around the mark equal to the height of the "i" figure's head (x) on all sides. No text, graphics, or busy imagery should enter this zone. This protects legibility at every size, from favicons to event backdrops.

Incorrect Usage

  • Do not stretch or distort the logo in any direction.
  • Do not recolor the mark outside the approved palette.
  • Do not place the logo on low-contrast or cluttered backgrounds.
  • Do not add outlines, heavy shadows, or effects to the mark.
  • Do not rotate or rearrange the cap, figure, or book.
  • Do not use low-resolution or outdated logo files.

Elements & Graphics

Supporting graphics keep the identity consistent and recognizable. They should support the message while maintaining a clean, modern, and professional look.

Halftone dot fields, used as corner and edge texture
Geometric diamond lattices in layered blues
Flowing wave linework for motion and progress
Fine grids and perspective planes for structure
Light-to-navy gradients for dark, formal layouts
White-to-blue gradients for light, airy layouts

Transparency usage: apply transparency to background images, graphics, shapes, and gradients to improve readability and balance. A level of 30%–50% is recommended so text, logos, and key content stay clear while the design remains clean and professional.

Brand Playbook

The complete Brand DNA and content manual for every current and future member of iSkolar: designers, marketers, volunteers, interns, sponsors, and partners.

Brand DNA

Every content produced by iSkolar should educate, empathize, or elevate. If it does none of these, rethink the publication.

Educate

Teach before selling. Make every content useful.

Empathize

Respect every student's reality without romanticizing hardship.

Elevate

Celebrate progress with transparency and gratitude.

Brand Voice
Student First Transparent Professional Friendly Credible Specific Warm Community Driven Evidence Based Hopeful without Hype
Caption DNA

Every caption should naturally follow the same storytelling flow.

1

Hook

Capture attention immediately.

2

Context

Explain why this matters.

3

Value

Teach, inspire, or inform.

4

Community

Invite students to belong.

5

Call to Action

Encourage readers to visit iskolar.io or join the community.

Content Strategy
Educational · 40% Community · 30% Product Updates · 20% Brand Awareness · 10%
Official Hashtag Guidelines
Primary
Secondary
  • Always prioritize primary hashtags.
  • Use only relevant secondary hashtags.
  • Use 3–8 hashtags per publication.
  • Avoid hashtag stuffing.
  • Avoid unrelated trending hashtags.
  • Technology hashtags should only appear on technology-related content.
  • Community posts should focus on community-related hashtags.
Branding Do's & Don'ts
✓ Do
  • Be student first.
  • Educate before selling.
  • Use a friendly, credible, transparent voice.
  • Be specific.
  • State what is live today and what is being built next.
  • Position iSkolar as the bridge connecting students, sponsors, and schools.
  • Communicate that iSkolar is free for students.
  • Explain blockchain accurately.
  • Separate fund transparency from selection fairness.
  • Frame iSkolar as another scholarship pathway.
  • Use English for institutional content and Taglish for student communities when appropriate.
  • Tell authentic stories with dignity.
  • Keep visibility strategic.
  • Build community over authority.
  • Earn trust through useful content.
  • Use personal accounts thoughtfully.
  • Label pilots honestly.
  • Redirect legal and technical questions to the CTO or CEO.
✕ Don't
  • Do not hard sell.
  • Do not use poverty porn.
  • Do not overpromise.
  • Do not exaggerate.
  • Never say iSkolar gives scholarships.
  • Never promise funding.
  • Do not claim blockchain guarantees fairness.
  • Do not claim to eliminate corruption.
  • Do not replace DOST or CHED.
  • Do not describe iSkolar as a crypto product.
  • Do not invent partnerships.
  • Do not misrepresent pilots.
  • Do not create rescue narratives.
  • Do not chase reach over credibility.
  • Do not sound inaccessible.
  • Do not answer beyond verified information.
Design Do's & Don'ts
✓ Do's
  • Use the official iSkolar logo, colors, and typography consistently.
  • Follow the approved color palette and typography hierarchy.
  • Maintain a clean, modern, and professional design style.
  • Use high-quality images, graphics, and illustrations.
  • Ensure all materials are student-centered and easy to understand.
  • Use sufficient white space to improve readability and balance.
  • Keep layouts organized and consistent across all platforms.
  • Align all designs with iSkolar's values of trust, innovation, and accessibility.
✕ Don'ts
  • Do not use unapproved fonts, colors, or logo variations.
  • Do not overcrowd designs with too many elements or effects.
  • Do not stretch, distort, or modify brand assets.
  • Do not use low-resolution images or graphics.
  • Do not mix different design styles within the same material.
  • Do not use colors that clash with the brand palette.
  • Do not create layouts that are difficult to read or navigate.
  • Do not use excessive gradients, shadows, or decorative effects that distract from the message.
Content Decision Tree

Run every idea through these seven questions. If any answer is no, rethink the publication.

1

Does this educate students?

2

Does this build trust?

3

Does this strengthen the community?

4

Can every claim be verified?

5

Does this respect student dignity?

6

Would this survive media, sponsor, or investor scrutiny?

7

Would we proudly publish this one year from now?
